e.t: This word describes something valuable—something regarded as having real worth. It functions as an adjective, adding this quality to a person, thing, activity, or teaching. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs four times across three verses, so its basic meaning remains focused and consistent rather than broad or specialized. The surrounding verse determines what is being called valuable, but the word itself points to worth and benefit rather than merely outward appearance or price.
